_note: The nurse safety suite, Wave 3: a timer on every visit, a panic button that shows the desk where a nurse is for a fixed window, and the desk queue that works both. MyThuso Master Blueprint v4's Engine 4 seed scope ships the 'nurse safety suite from day one', and ThusoIQ Master v3.5 section 58 item 4 names what it must hold: 'check-in/check-out on every visit, panic button and live location to the ops desk'. This file holds the states, the numbers and the refusal sentences; packages/engines/src/safety/domain holds the arithmetic; scripts/emit-field-safety.mjs writes both native copies. Nothing here is a running service. No timer reaches a desk, no panic reaches a person, no position is read from a device, and the nurse-position door in packages/catalog/feeds.json stays shut.
_numbersNote: Two of the numbers below are decided and two are still proposals. The founder decided the grace and the panic window on 15 September 2026 — "panic 30, grace 60" — and that Operations changes them on the admin rather than in code; each carries decidedBy, decidedOn and why, in the shape packages/catalog/consent.json gives maximumExpiryDecision. The extension steps and ceiling were not part of that decision and keep `decidedBy: null`, which means nobody with the authority to set them has: ThusoIQ Master v3.5's readiness review (58A) marks 'Nurse workforce & field safety' RED, and its next step is to 'approve employment/flex model, caseload, pay, routing, buddy/no-go rules and panic/escort policy'. The build refuses a proposal that loses its `decidedBy` key and a decision that loses who took it or when, so a number cannot quietly become policy by having the question deleted around it. Each value here is the default; settings below says what an admin may change it to.

timer.whyFromTheService: A visit is timed by the service that was booked. A number typed on a screen or sent with a request is a timer that can be set to anything; the duration in the catalogue is the one the patient was quoted and the nurse's day is drawn from.

graceMinutes.why: The founder decided on 15 September 2026, "panic 30, grace 60", and that Operations sets it on the admin. The desk is told an hour after a visit's booked duration, and any extensions she took, if the nurse has not checked out. An hour means a visit that runs long for an ordinary reason — a family with questions, a dressing that takes longer than booked — does not page the desk, so a page from the desk still means something. The cost is written here so that it is read: a nurse in trouble who cannot press panic is looked for up to an hour after she should have left. A nurse who can press panic does not wait for the grace at all.
graceMinutes.question: How long after a visit's booked duration the desk is told a nurse has not checked out.

extensionMinutes.proposedBecause: Three choices a nurse can press with one hand at a door, rather than a number field.
extensionMinutes.question: The extensions a nurse may choose from.

maxExtensionMinutes.proposedBecause: An hour beyond the booked time is as long as a visit should run before a person at the desk speaks to the nurse, whatever the reason.
maxExtensionMinutes.question: The most a visit may be extended in total before only the desk can let it run on.

windowMinutes.why: The founder decided on 15 September 2026, "panic 30, grace 60", and that Operations sets it on the admin. The desk sees a nurse's position for thirty minutes after she presses panic: enough to pick the panic up, reach her and let a person at the desk decide whether to send somebody, and no longer, because every minute a position is shown is a minute somebody is watching where a nurse is. The window does not stretch: a nurse who still needs help when it ends presses again and a new window starts, which leaves the desk a record of both rather than one share quietly made longer.
windowMinutes.question: How long the desk sees a nurse's position after she presses panic.

panic.confirmQuestion: Alert the desk that you need help?
panic.whatHappens: The desk is alerted and can see where you are until {ends}. Nobody else can: not the patient, not other nurses, and not any other part of MyThuso.
panic.whatDoesNotHappen: Pressing panic does not call the police or an ambulance. A person at the desk decides that. If you can, call {police} for the police or {ambulance} for an ambulance yourself.
panic._emergencyNumbersNote: {police} and {ambulance} are the numbers in packages/catalog/sos.json, filled in by the domain rules on the web and by scripts/emit-field-safety.mjs for the native apps. An emergency number typed twice is one that can be typed wrong twice.
panic.sharingUntil: The desk can see your position until {ends}.
panic.sharingStopped: The desk stopped seeing your position at {ended}.
panic.pressAgain: If you still need help, press panic again. A new window starts.
panic.sameVisit: A second press by the same nurse for the same visit while its window is open is the same panic, answered again. It is never refused, and a press by anybody else is never folded into it.

simulation.why: How often the simulated feed produces a position while a window is open. It is the simulation's cadence, not a policy: no device reports anything, and the feed is generated on the machine that draws the desk.
simulation.positionRule: The simulated position is the centre of the suburb the nurse works in, at the precision packages/catalog/geography.json declares. It is never the patient's address, because the preview has no address to give.

settings._note: The founder decided on 15 September 2026 that Operations changes the field-safety timings on the admin, without a code change: "Safety: 30min, grace 60min - but configure this on the admin". A number still lives in one place. The default is where it always was, in timer and panic above; this block holds, for each timing an admin may change, where that default is, the lowest and highest an admin may set, the unit and who may change it, the sentences the admin screen shows, and the record of every change to the defaults themselves. What is in force at any moment is the defaults with every accepted admin change replayed in order: kept in the Safety engine's own store by packages/engines/src/safety, and in the web preview in the tab's memory.
settings._changeableByNote: The admin role in packages/catalog/vetting.json, calling POST /v1/safety/setting-changes@1 for the audit purpose, as the incident register's admin routes in packages/catalog/apis/safety.json do. No capability on the register names changing the desk's timings, so none is claimed: the engine runtime admits the role from the contract and nothing more, and a production door has to decide which capability this is.
settings._versionNote: Two versions, and they are different things. defaults.version counts changes to this file, replayed by the build like packages/catalog/gilbert-emergency-terms.json. settingsVersion counts changes an admin made at runtime, starting at 1 for these defaults; a visit timer and a panic keep the settingsVersion they started under, so a change never reaches back into one already running.
settings._careOfferExpiryNote: Care's offer expiry is not on this screen. It is Care's number in packages/catalog/care.json and Care's engine enforces it; Safety's store holding it would be one engine keeping another's policy. Putting it on the admin needs a Care settings route of its own.

lowest.proposedBecause: The fifteen minutes first proposed on 14 September. Below it the desk is paged for visits that are only running a little over, and a desk paged for nothing learns to ignore the page.

highest.proposedBecause: Twice the founder's hour. Past two hours after her booked time a nurse in trouble who cannot press panic is looked for in the afternoon for a morning visit, and moving it that far is a decision for this contract rather than a setting on a screen.

lowest.proposedBecause: Shorter than fifteen minutes is shorter than the desk needs to pick a panic up, reach the nurse and send somebody, so the window would end while help was still being arranged.

highest.proposedBecause: The hour first proposed on 14 September. A position shown for longer than that is nearer to tracking a nurse than helping her, and a nurse who still needs help presses again and opens a new window.

lowest.proposedBecause: A step shorter than five minutes is a snooze rather than an extension, and a snooze is what extension-without-reason exists to refuse.

highest.proposedBecause: The largest step first proposed. One press that adds more than half an hour is a visit being rebooked at the door, which is a conversation for the desk.

timings.label: Most a visit may be extended

lowest.proposedBecause: Half an hour, so that the largest step the range allows can still be taken once.

highest.proposedBecause: Two hours beyond the booked time is as long as a visit should run on a nurse's own word under any setting. Past that a person at the desk speaks to her.

screen.heading: Field safety settings
screen.intro: How long the desk waits after a visit's booked time before it looks for a nurse, how long it sees her after a panic, and how much longer she may ask for. Operations changes them here, without a code change.
screen.appliesFrom: A change applies to visits and panics that start after it. A visit already running keeps its deadline, and a panic window already open keeps its end.
screen.range: An admin may set {lowest} to {highest} min
screen.rangeIsAProposal: The range is a proposal nobody has decided.
screen.newSteps: New steps in minutes, smallest first, separated by commas
screen.reasonHelp: Written into the history beside your name. It is read when somebody asks why the desk waited as long as it did.
screen.historyEmpty: Nothing has been changed from these defaults yet.
screen.historyNeverEdited: Every change is added here with who made it, when and why. Nothing here is edited or removed.
screen.preview: This preview keeps changes in this tab's memory and nowhere else. No nurse's phone and no desk is told, and a reload puts the defaults back.

changelog.by: Safety lead (Wave 3), proposed and not decided
changelog.why: The first proposals, so the nurse's strip and the desk could be built and tested against something.
"Safety: 30min, grace 60min - but configure this on the admin", clarified as "panic 30, grace 60". The extension steps and ceiling were not part of the decision and stay proposals.

howToChange: Change a default in timer or panic above, never here.

Raise defaults.version by one and add a changelog entry with the same version, the day, who made the change by role, every timing changed as { timing, from, to }, and why. npm run check replays the changelog from nothing and fails if it does not arrive at the defaults above.
A decided default names who decided it and on what day beside its value. A default nobody decided keeps decidedBy: null and says why it was proposed.
Every default stays inside its own lowest and highest. Moving a range is a change to this file, and the range is a proposal until somebody decides it.

timer.label: On a visit
timer.means: The timer is counting down to when she should have checked out.

timer.label: Past check-out
timer.means: The time plus the grace has passed and she has neither checked out nor extended.

timer.label: Checked out
timer.means: She checked out, or the visit was completed and signed.

panic.label: Waiting for the desk
panic.means: Pressed, and nobody at the desk has picked it up.

panic.label: The desk has it
panic.means: A person at the desk has picked it up.

panic.label: Resolved
panic.means: The desk recorded what happened. Sharing has stopped.

extensionReasons.label: The visit is taking longer than booked
Waiting for the patient or the family
Waiting for a doctor to call back

_extensionReasonsNote: A reason is what the desk reads beside an extended timer, so none of them says anything about the patient's health. 'Waiting for a doctor to call back' names who, never why.

silenceReasons.label: I reached the nurse by phone and she is safe
The nurse checked in, extended or checked out herself
A colleague confirmed she is safe

outcomes.label: Safe after the desk spoke to her
A person at the desk called the police or an ambulance
Pressed by mistake, confirmed with the nurse

nurse.heading: Your safety
nurse.left: {minutes} min left. If you have not checked out by then, the desk is told.
nurse.overdue: Past check-out since {since}. The desk has been told.
nurse.answered: You said you were safe at {at}.
nurse.closedBySigning: Checked out when the visit was signed at {at}.
nurse.extendQuestion: Why do you need more time?
nurse.extendLeft: Up to {minutes} more minutes can be added to this visit.

desk.heading: Nurses in the field
desk.empty: No nurse is past check-out and nobody has pressed panic. The queue fills itself; there is nothing to refresh.
desk.waiting: {waiting} waiting to be picked up · {open} open
desk.reasonQuestion: Why is it safe to close?

neverCarries.why: What the visit was for is clinical. A queue of 'Family planning' and 'Mental-health check-in' rows is a disclosure to everybody standing behind the desk.
The desk needs to know which nurse and which suburb. The patient's name is in the visit, for the nurse, not on a board.
geography.json's address-is-not-a-pin, read at the desk: a suburb is enough to send somebody, and the nurse's position is shown during a panic and nowhere else.

desk.order: A panic nobody has picked up, then a timer nobody has picked up, then everything the desk already has. Oldest first inside each.

refusals.statement: A visit whose code did not match has not started, so it has no timer.
refusals.why: appointment.in_progress carries visitCodeMatched so that a subscriber can refuse one that says otherwise.

refusals.statement: That visit's service is not in the catalogue, so there is nothing to time it by.
refusals.why: A timer with a guessed duration is a timer that fires at the wrong time.

refusals.statement: An extension says why, in one of the reasons the desk can read.
refusals.why: The desk decides whether to call from the reason. An extension with none is a snooze.

refusals.statement: Extensions come in the steps the desk offers.
refusals.why: A free number is how a timer is set to a day.

refusals.statement: That visit is checked out. Nothing is being timed.
refusals.why: A closed timer does not reopen; a new visit starts a new one.

refusals.statement: An overdue check-in is closed with a reason, or it stays open.
refusals.why: An alarm silenced without a reason is an alarm somebody made stop.

refusals.statement: The nurse has not checked in, extended or checked out, so that cannot be the reason.
refusals.why: The reason is checked against the timer, not taken on trust.

refusals.statement: That check-in is not overdue, so there is nothing here for the desk.
refusals.why: A reason recorded against nothing is noise in the record.

refusals.statement: Somebody at the desk picks an overdue check-in up before it is closed.
refusals.why: The record has to say that a person saw it, for a timer exactly as for a panic.

refusals.statement: This position is no longer shared. Sharing ended at {ended}.
refusals.why: The window always ends, and the desk is told when rather than shown the last place she was.

refusals.statement: A panic is resolved with what happened, or it stays open.
refusals.why: A panic closed with no outcome leaves nothing to review. ThusoIQ Master v3.5 section 55 names an incident review within 24 hours for harm to a patient or responder during a Thuso Ride trip; holding a nurse's panic to the same review is this contract's proposal, not the document's, and it needs the outcome written down.

refusals.statement: Somebody at the desk picks a panic up before it is resolved.
refusals.why: The record has to say that a person saw it.

refusals.statement: That panic is already resolved. If she needs help again, a new panic starts.
refusals.why: A resolved panic does not reopen, and its window does not come back.

refusals.statement: The window does not stretch. A nurse who still needs help presses panic again.
refusals.why: A share that can be extended from the desk is a share with no end.

refusals.statement: A position is gone when sharing stops. Nothing keeps where she was.
refusals.why: geography.json's no-history-drawn: a safety feature that keeps positions is a tracking system.

_routeRefusalsNote: Refusals that already belong to a route are named by route and id and read from packages/catalog/apis/safety.json, so the sentence the API returns and the sentence a screen shows are one string.
